issue_context.title: Set PG Backend Connection String through an environment variable.
issue_context.body:
### Current Terraform Version

Version 0.14.x

### Use-cases

I would like to be able to set the connection string for the PostgreSQL backend using an environment variable. Currently, an environment variable doesn't work for that setting.

### Attempted Solutions

I tried setting several different combinations of the environment variable without any results.

### Proposal
Add the DefaultFunc property to ready the environment variable like what happens in the Azure, GCS, and S3 backends. Here is the S3 for example.

```
DefaultFunc: schema.EnvDefaultFunc("AWS_DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT", ""),
```

I propose adding the following DefaultFunc for the pg backend conn_str property.

```
DefaultFunc: schema.EnvDefaultFunc("PG_CONN_STR", ""),
```
comments: @phillipsj would you consider creating the PR as-is? Changing the name of the variable is relatively effortless, so maybe that'd help get some added attention to the PR. 👍
@phillipsj this change looks like a good idea to me!

Interestingly, the current [pg backend documentation](https://www.terraform.io/language/settings/backends/pg) states that "The following configuration options **or environment variables** are supported: `conn_str` [...]". 

But I have not managed to figure out how it's done. What is supposed to be the environment variable to set `conn_str` or any other back-end configuration?

The only workaround I found to pass a pg connection string to Terraform is rather ugly: ` TF_CLI_ARGS="-backend-config='conn_str=postgres://some_host/some_db'"`.
@phillipsj why did you close your PR and now this issue?
@rook59 this issue and PR has been open over a year. The rebase was going to take more effort than I wanted to provide considering how long this issue and PR sat without any movement.
